meta.title: Tan War
supplies: Pencil and paper, or markers for tracks
About 80 small tokens or the printed counter sheet

brief.conflict: Irish War of Independence, 1919 to 1921: a guerrilla war between the Irish Republican Army and British forces.

overview.period: 21 January 1919 to a truce on 11 July 1921.
actors: Irish Republican Army and the Dail government
Royal Irish Constabulary with Black and Tans and Auxiliaries

sources.title: Irish War of Independence (Wikipedia)
sources.readScope: Characters 0 to 100000 of 189438. The rest was not read.

sources.title: Timeline of the Irish War of Independence (Wikipedia)

claims.text: The war began with the Soloheadbeg ambush on 21 January 1919 and ended with a truce on 11 July 1921.
The first Black and Tans arrived in March 1920 and the Auxiliaries in July 1920.
Bloody Sunday took place in Dublin on 21 November 1920.
claims.conflict: The article gives 14 British dead in one place and 16 in another.

claims.text: Martial law began in much of Munster on 10 December 1920.
A truce took effect in July 1921.
The eight spaces and their Pop values are proposed design values, not historical measurements.
Opinion levels (Support, Neutral, Opposition) and the Repression track are design abstractions.
Event card effects are original design, loosely themed on the period.

factions.name: Crown
factions.role: Holds towns and roads. Pays to place forces. Wins by turning opinion toward the Crown.

factions.name: Republic
factions.role: Hides among the people. Pays little. Wins by turning opinion toward the Republic and holding Headquarters.

sequence.firstActor: The leftmost Eligible faction on the card's symbol row acts first. If only one faction is Eligible, it acts alone and may choose Event, Operation plus Special Activity, Operation only or Pass.

eligibilityAfter.bothIneligibleResult: If both factions would be Ineligible, both stay Eligible.

phases.name: Victory check
phases.text: Compute each faction's victory score. If one or more factions exceed their threshold, the game ends. On the final Truce Talks card the game ends whatever the scores. The highest margin wins.

phases.name: Income
phases.text: Crown gains 2 Resources plus 1 per Barracks on the map. Republic gains 1 Resource plus 1 per HQ on the map.

phases.name: Reset
phases.text: Flip all Active Volunteers to Underground. Make both factions Eligible.

text.overview: Tan War is a two-faction game of insurgency. Crown holds towns and pays for every action. Republic hides among the people and strikes when odds are good. Both factions fight over opinion in eight spaces.
text.components: Eight spaces on the board. Crown pieces: 12 Army, 12 Police, 4 Barracks. Republic pieces: 16 Volunteers, 5 HQs. Tracks: Crown Resources, Republic Resources, Repression. One die. 10 cards: 8 Event cards and 2 Truce Talks cards.
text.setup: Follow the setup sheet. Place pieces and set opinion in each space. Set the three tracks. Prepare the deck as the deck section says.
text.sequence: Reveal the top card. Factions act in the order shown on the card, as the sequence table says. Each faction that acts chooses from the options the table allows. Operations cost Resources. A Special Activity may follow an Operation.
text.operations: Each Operation costs the faction's Resources per chosen space. A Limited Operation uses 1 space and no Special Activity. See the faction aids for each action.
text.events: An Event card has two sides. The acting faction picks either side. Event text overrides these rules, except that piece limits always hold.
text.scoring: A Truce Talks card runs four phases in order: victory check, income, calm, reset.
text.victory: Crown wins with 9 or more Support Pop. Republic wins with 10 or more Opposition Pop plus HQs. Check at each Truce Talks card. After the final card, the highest margin wins. Ties go to Republic.
text.solo: Use the bot aid for each faction you do not play. Follow the flowchart in order. Roll the die only when the aid says to.

actions.name: Garrison
actions.plain: In each chosen city or Barracks space, place up to 2 Army and 1 Police from Available.
actions.purpose: Add Crown forces in cities and Barracks.

actions.name: Sweep
actions.plain: In each chosen space with an Underground Volunteer, move up to 3 Army in from adjacent spaces. Then flip one Underground Volunteer to Active for each Army and Police there.

actions.name: Crackdown
actions.plain: In each chosen space with Crown cubes, remove Active Volunteers up to the number of Army and Police there. Then remove an HQ if no Volunteers remain.

actions.name: Martial Law
actions.plain: In one space with 2 or more Army and opinion below Support, shift opinion one step toward the Crown. Then raise Repression by 1 and place a Curfew marker there. The marker records Crown rule; it has no other effect.

actions.name: Rally
actions.plain: In each chosen space with a Volunteer or HQ, choose: place Volunteers (2 with an HQ, otherwise 1) or replace 2 Volunteers with an HQ if none is there. If Repression is 3 or more, place 1 extra Volunteer.
actions.purpose: Add Volunteers or build an HQ.

actions.name: March
actions.plain: Into each chosen space, move any number of Volunteers from adjacent spaces. Moved Volunteers become Active if Army or Police are in the destination.

actions.name: Attack
actions.plain: In one chosen space with Volunteers and Crown cubes, roll one die. On a roll at or below the number of Volunteers there, remove 1 Crown cube (Army first). Then flip all Underground Volunteers there to Active.

actions.name: Boycott
actions.plain: In one space with 2 or more Underground Volunteers and opinion above Opposition, shift opinion one step toward the Republic.

cards.title: Flying Column
cards.flavor: Small mobile units strike and vanish.

sides.label: Intelligence
sides.text: Crown: in one space with a Crown cube, remove all Active Volunteers.

sides.label: Ambush
sides.text: Republic: place 2 Underground Volunteers in a space with an HQ.

sides.label: Reinforced Posts
sides.text: Crown: place 2 Police from Available in each of 2 cities.

sides.label: Backlash
sides.text: Republic: shift opinion one step toward the Republic in up to 2 spaces with 2 or more Police.

cards.title: Restoration of Order
cards.flavor: Emergency law replaces juries with courts-martial.

cards.title: Bloody Sunday
cards.flavor: A morning of killings in the capital.

sides.label: Dublin Sweep
sides.text: Crown: remove up to 2 Volunteers from Dublin.

sides.label: Public Outrage
sides.text: Republic: shift Dublin opinion one step toward the Republic. Repression rises by 2.

cards.title: Republican Courts
cards.flavor: A parallel justice system draws local trust.

sides.label: Shut the Courts
sides.text: Crown: remove 1 HQ from a space with no Underground Volunteers.

sides.label: Courts Sit
sides.text: Republic: shift opinion one step toward the Republic in a space with an HQ.

cards.title: Arms from America
cards.flavor: Money and rifles cross the sea.

sides.label: Shipment Lands
sides.text: Republic: gain 3 Resources. Move 2 Volunteers from Out of Play to Available.

sides.label: Troops Arrive
sides.text: Crown: move 2 Army from Out of Play to Available. Then place 2 Army in a city.

sides.label: Resentment
sides.text: Republic: lower Repression by 2 and gain 1 Resource.

sides.label: Calm Returns
sides.text: Crown: shift one space with Crown cubes one step toward the Crown.

sides.label: Hope Spreads
sides.text: Republic: shift one space with Underground Volunteers one step toward the Republic.

cards.title: Truce Talks
cards.flavor: Both sides count what they hold.

cards.title: Truce Talks (Final)
cards.flavor: The last count before a settlement.

preparation.text: Make two piles. Pile 1: shuffle the first four Event cards (E01 to E04) and put Truce Talks (S1) into the bottom three positions. Pile 2: shuffle E05 to E08 and put the final Truce Talks (S2) at the bottom. Put Pile 1 on top of Pile 2.

victory.checkAt: Each Truce Talks card, in the victory check phase.
victory.finalScoring: After the final Truce Talks card, the faction with the highest margin (score minus threshold) wins.
tieBreaks: Republic wins a tie in margin.
A bot faction wins ties before a human faction.

bots.objective: Win by raising Crown Support Pop to 9: Pop of spaces at Support. Remove Active Volunteers first, then place forces in valuable neutral cities, then sweep. Keep Resources for Garrison and Martial Law.

measures.name: Support Pop
measures.plain: Total Pop of spaces at Support.

measures.name: Exposed
measures.plain: A space is exposed if it holds an Active Volunteer and at least 1 Crown cube.

measures.name: Valuable
measures.plain: A space is valuable if its Pop is 2 or more and opinion is below Support.

eventPolicy.plain: Play the unshaded side if the Event has an effect and it raises Crown Support Pop or lowers Republic score. Otherwise do not play it.

overrides.plain: Play Flying Column only if a space holds an Active Volunteer and a Crown cube.
Always play Martial Law Decree when it has an effect, even with Event value 0.

randomization.eligibleSet: All spaces still tied after the lettered tie-breaks, listed in alphabetical order of space name.
randomization.procedure: Roll one die. With N tied spaces, divide the die faces into N equal groups in list order (for 2 spaces: 1 to 3 picks the first, 4 to 6 picks the second). Use the group the roll falls in.
